description.narrative: The Guinea Power Recovery Project objective is to improve the technical and commercial performance of the national power utility. The proposed project is designed to restore the viability of the Guinean energy sector based on the recommendations of the Power Sector Diagnostic and Recovery Plan adopted by the Government. Though currently performing poorly, the Guinean power system could become financially sustainable in the medium term. Such a turnaround is only possible if: (i) sector governance were improved, (ii) electricity losses (technical and commercial) were reduced; (ii) efficient sector maintenance and investment were enforced; and (iii) additional resources were to be mobilized from donors and increasingly from the private sector to accelerate the implementation of rehabilitation and system development investment, and energy conservation measures. The project is structured around three main components: (1) Financing of a Management Services Contract to support EDG performance improvement, (2) Selected investments to support improvement of Conakry distribution network and commercial performance of EDG, (3) Technical assistance to MEH and project implementation support.
The Project Development Objective (PDO) is to improve the technical and commercial performance of the national power utility.

comment.narrative: <p><strong>Exceeded</strong>: The customer base for the electricity utility (EDG) grew by 266% from 240,690 in 2015 to 638,301 at the end of the first quarter of 2022, following major actions carried out within the framework of the PRSP, including the customer census operation, the regularization of connections and implementation of anti-fraud policies. This indicator was based on the following criteria: (i) 79% of subscribers are households; (ii) a household has 8 people; and (iii) the customer base at the end of the second quarter of 2022 was 638,301 active customers. The last population and housing census consider that 52% of the Guinean population are women, and 52% of the population benefiting from electricity services are women.</p>

<p><strong>Exceeded</strong>: As part of the implementation of the RMT contract in the Municipality of Dixinn, 22 substations, which have all been rehabilitated. The rehabilitation of these substations has considerably reduced the losses in this municipality, but also the breakage of transformers which were often overloaded.</p>

title.narrative: People provided with new or improved electricity service

comment.narrative: <p><strong>Exceeded:</strong> Achievement rate for this indicator is 131%. This indicator is calculated taking into account two elements: (i) the number of connections made by RMT and CEGELEC (43,441), Société Togo Assistance Services – TAS (17,000) and HEXING within the framework of income protection (5,454), i.e. a total of 65,895 connections made, (ii) 79% of customers are households according to the EDG’s estimates.</p>

title.narrative: Distribution lines constructed or rehabilitated under the project

comment.narrative: <p><strong>Exceeded</strong>: This activity was entrusted to the constructor RMT which evolved in the Municipality of Dixinn. The target for this indicator was met.</p>

<p><strong>Exceeded</strong>: Results were due to: (i) iincrease in hydro and thermal production capacity, through the commissioning of hydroelectric power stations in Kaléta (240 MW) and Souapiti (450 MW) and the thermal power stations in Kaloum 1 to 5, Kipé, Té-Power and Kar Power, (ii) the rehabilitation of the hydroelectric power plants of the Samou system made it possible to recover non-functional groups for years. Electricity production increased from 92.43 GWh at the end of 2015 to 844 GWh in March 2022.</p>

<p><strong>Exceeded</strong>: The target for this indicator was exceeded, and the actions that led to this appreciable result are summarized as follows: (i) On the technical level, the project carried out the rehabilitation of the electricity distribution network, rehabilitation and standardization of connections in the Municipalities of Dixinn, Ratoma, Matoto and Kaloum, the construction of the substation of Kissosso as well as the construction of 39 cabin stations and the rehabilitation of 22 cabin stations in the Municipality of Dixinn; (ii) At the commercial level, the project funded the installation of 65,895 meters and the connections in the agencies of Dixinn, Lamabanyi, Matoto, Kissosso, Kipé, Taouyah, Yimpbaya, Tombolia, Matam, Coléyah and Kaloum, which made it possible to considerably reduce non-technical (commercial) losses.</p>

<p><strong>Partially achieved</strong>: The overall recovery rate is 86% as of March 31, 2022, including 72% recovery from private subscribers. This rate could improve with the recovery of private arrears and would exceed 95%.</p>

title.narrative: Average interruption frequency per year in the project area

comment.narrative: <p><strong>Exceeded</strong>: The parameters used by EDG to calculate this indicator are: SAIFI (frequency of interruptions) and SAIDI (frequency of outages). At the end of March 2022, these parameters were 35 and 26 respectively.</p>

<p><strong>Fully Achieved</strong>: The VEOLIA / SEURECA consortium was competitively selected for a period of 4 years. The Contract ended on October 9, 2019. An interim team had been appointed before the finalization of the recruitment process, financed by the project, including the Director General, eleven Sector Directors and 36 Heads of Department.</p>

<p><strong>Fully Achieved</strong>: The selected auditor carried out half-yearly and quarterly audit missions and carried out various reviews of the EDG Internal Recovery Plan. All the deliverables developed under the Management Contract as well as EDG's Internal Recovery Plan (PRI) recommended by the Government were assessed by the auditor. These deliverables by the auditor led to the production of review reports.</p>

title.narrative: Average number of hours of training per staff per year

comment.narrative: <p>Since the departure of the operator VEOLIA, this indicator has not been calculated, because a vast capacity building program was in preparation, of which only the catalog training component was carried out</p>

title.narrative: People provided with access to electricity services under the project by household connections rehabilitation and standardization of household connections in Kaloum Ratoma and Matoto

comment.narrative: <p><strong>Exceeded</strong>: the achievement rate for this indicator is 157%, justified by the following achievements: (i) Number of connections made by the manufacturer CEGELEC in these municipalities: 34,028; (ii) Number of connections made by HEXING under thePPR: 4038- Number of connections made by RMT in households in Lambanyi: 15,781. The total number of connections made by these manufacturers is 53,847. Considering that 79% of customers are households, we have 340,313 connections under the Project.</p>
<p><strong>Exceeded</strong>: As part of the RMT Contract in the Municipality of Dixinn, it was planned to build 39 stations instead of 24.</p>

title.narrative: People provided with access to electricity services under the project by household connections Rehabilitation and extension of Distribution network in Dixinn

comment.narrative: <p><strong>Practically exceeded</strong>. This indicator was calculated assuming that 79% of customers are households. The Builder RMT made 9413 connections and HEXING made 477. It is important to note that RMT made all the quantity planned under its Contract. Considering the meters already installed by EDG and the installations in progress, this indicator would be reached and even exceeded.</p>

title.narrative: Number of meters installed, of which large consumer smart meters

comment.narrative: <p><strong>Exceeded</strong>: The target was met for this indicator. These meters were installed as follows: 9,413 by RMT, 34,028 by CEGELEC, 5,454 by HEXING and 17,000 meters by TAS.</p>
